title: Ariel and Caliban comparison grid
subject: English
unit: Spring 2: The Tempest (Shakespeare): transformation through forgiveness
source: Written for english/y7 lesson 31 (Ariel and Caliban comparison grid (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 31: Ariel, Caliban and freedom (Act 1 scene 2 and Act 2). Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

head: Ariel
Caliban
rows: born on the island, son of Sycorax

passage.title: Caliban, The Tempest, Act 1 scene 2
paras: This island's mine, by Sycorax my mother,

panels.title: Act 2: a new master and false freedom
points: Stephano gives him wine; Caliban becomes foolish
He swaps one master for a worse one
He sings of freedom while still a servant

keywords.def: the power to act and choose for yourself
a character who contrasts with another to highlight their qualities
a particular way of seeing events

questions.q: Write a PETZAAL paragraph opening (Point, Evidence, Zoom in): 'How does Shakespeare present Caliban's feelings about the island?'
questions.a: For example: Caliban feels robbed: 'This island's mine', where 'mine' shows his sense of ownership.

questions.q: In one sentence each, explain how Ariel and Caliban want freedom differently.
questions.a: Ariel earns freedom through obedient service; Caliban wants it by rebelling and plotting.

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, write a PETZAAL paragraph: 'How does Shakespeare present the theme of freedom through Ariel and Caliban?' Starter: 'Shakespeare uses Ariel and Caliban to...'
questions.a: A comparative PETZAAL paragraph with one short quotation for each character and an Alternative.

questions.q: Extend: is Prospero fair to Caliban? One reason for, one against.
questions.a: For: Caliban broke Prospero's trust. Against: Prospero took the island and rules by force.

questions.q: Stretch: what does the Act 2 scene with Stephano suggest about false freedom?
questions.a: That swapping one master for another, while drunk, is not true freedom.

questions.q: Why is Ariel a foil to Caliban?
options: Ariel's willing service highlights Caliban's resentment
They both want to be king
questions.a: A) Ariel's willing service highlights Caliban's resentment. Foils contrast to highlight qualities; B and C are untrue.

questions.q: Who claims the island through his mother?
Answer the ponder in one sentence with a reason.
questions.a: For example: no, because service without consent becomes servitude, even after a kindness.
